insights.title: Protect the core 5 Series delighter: refined, quiet driving pleasure
insights.description: Customers still describe the 5 Series’ fundamental appeal as a premium car that is fun, smooth, quick, quiet and comfortable to drive. This is the strongest delighter to keep while improving other pain points.
vfc_topics: Drive, driving dynamics and chassis, overall technology

evidence.detail: "drives beautifully. it stays nice and quiet when you want that, but turns genuinely sporty"
"fantastic to drive. smooth and quick. cabin is quiet and very comfortable"
"bmw puts the driver first and i realy like that"
"at highway speeds, the vehicle's handling does not feel as stable as his 2019 5 Series"
"the drive is fantastic, but a firmer, more responsive suspension would be better"

conflicting_signals: The same US feedback set contains strong driving praise and complaints about stability, responsiveness or ride harshness, especially versus prior BMWs.
CN support comes from study data only; there are no CN verbatims.
data_gaps: No CN customer feedback verbatims to explain what specifically drives high CN roadholding and sportiness scores.
The study is not split by powertrain, so differences between ICE, PHEV and BEV driving satisfaction are inferred mainly from verbatims.

insights.title: EV owners need range and charging confidence, not just good electric driving
insights.description: BEV and PHEV customers often like the car itself but want more predictable real-world range, reliable scheduled home charging, clearer fast-charging information and easier public charging access for long trips.

evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

"begin charging at a certain time at night without having to enter a departure time"
"the app to clearly show how much power in kw is being charged... fast charging stations should stand out"
"would like higher charging speeds so he spends less time at charging stations"
For a successor launching in 3-5 years, EV trip-planning and charging-network expectations are likely to rise versus today.

conflicting_signals: US and EU evidence shows range/charging anxiety, while CN fuel economy/energy efficiency is strong in the study and has no verbatims to qualify it.
Home charging scheduling complaints and public charging complaints are different problems but combine into one customer perception: the EV is less effortless than it should be.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims or CN public-charging feedback are available.
No objective cold-weather range, charging-session success rate or public-network availability data is provided by market.
Feedback is concentrated in US BEV/PHEV owners; EU EV verbatim evidence is limited.

insights.title: Digital reliability must feel as premium as the vehicle hardware
insights.description: Owners’ trust is undermined when screens go black, app sync drops, CarPlay connects to the wrong phone, or Digital Key behavior creates lock/unlock surprises. Customers expect the connected ecosystem to be robust, profile-aware and predictable.

evidence.detail: "the screen going completely black for around a day and a half"
"keeps dropping the connection so the app is out of sync"
"often grabs the last phone it used, which can be different from whoever is driving"
"wireless CarPlay will occasionally not connect"
"his phone with the Digital Key was locked inside"
"i really like the digital key"

conflicting_signals: Some US owners praise Digital Key and app-related features, while others experience failures that feel disproportionate in a premium car.
CN and EU connected-services scores are relatively low in their study lists, but no verbatims are available for CN and only limited EU verbatims are available.
data_gaps: No diagnostic frequency data for black screens, app desynchronization, CarPlay failures or Digital Key lock cases.
No CN verbatims to explain the Connected services score.

insights.title: Premium cabin perception is vulnerable to perceived cost cutting
insights.description: Some owners, especially in the US verbatims, say the cabin no longer feels premium enough because of hard plastics, reduced leather or equipment, seat comfort issues and missing familiar seat controls. Seating and material quality remain core luxury cues.

evidence.detail: "interior feels like a step down from the previous model in both materials and equipment"
"excess of cheap-feeling, hard plastic components"
"more premium materials in the cabin and less plastic overall"
"getting the driver seat adjusted so i do not end up with serious pain in my lower"
"multi contour seats with dedicated buttons... would like that same setup again"
evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

conflicting_signals: Study scores for seating comfort are good in CN and EU and acceptable-to-good in the US, while US verbatims contain sharp complaints about seat comfort, materials and deleted equipment.
Some comments praise comfort and materials, so the pain point appears concentrated among customers comparing with prior BMWs or rival luxury interiors.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims on cabin material expectations despite China being in scope.
No trim-level or option-content data to separate base-equipment dissatisfaction from actual quality perception.

insights.title: Customers want usable space, not just a large exterior
insights.description: Owners ask for practical space that works in daily life: trunk depth and pass-through, small-item storage, rear leg room for clients, easier entry and easier loading. US comments say the car can feel large outside while still compromised inside; EU study results also show luggage/loading and rear-roominess weaknesses.

insights.description: Styling remains a draw, yet some US owners say the car feels too long, too wide, harder to park or garage, or less sporty/too boxy. Exterior details such as badging and chrome can also affect whether the car feels premium rather than tacky.

insights.title: Braking and low-speed transitions must feel smooth and confidence-inspiring across powertrains
insights.description: Some customers want stronger, smoother and more consistent braking and stop/start behavior. Complaints include weak brake feel, grabby stops, brake noise/dust, different PHEV brake feel between electric and combustion modes, and non-smooth automatic start-stop transitions.

evidence.detail: "brakes don't come across as strong enough"
"braking... feels terrible, like it's grabbing... impossible to come to a stop smoothly"
evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

evidence.detail: "braking feels lighter in electric mode... would prefer a more seamless transition"
evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

evidence.detail: "squeaking sound from the brakes after only about four weeks"
"auto engine start-stop feature leads to a not-smooth transition"

conflicting_signals: CN braking score is comparatively low in its study list, while EU and US braking study scores are stronger than the negative US verbatims suggest.
ICE, PHEV and BEV complaints differ: start-stop smoothness for ICE/mild hybrid, blended braking transition for PHEV, and stopping confidence for heavier electrified vehicles.
data_gaps: No CN verbatims to explain the low CN braking score.
No objective brake feel, noise, dust or blended-brake transition measurements by powertrain.

insight_caveats: No customer feedback verbatims are available for China; CN conclusions rely on the customer study, sales data where cited, and stated assumptions only.
The provided verbatim sample is heavily US-weighted; EU verbatim evidence is limited and no CN verbatim evidence is available.
279 verbatims from outside CN/EU/US are excluded from market-specific interpretation, per the data package.
Customer-study attributes differ by market, especially US versus CN/EU scales, so cross-market comparisons should be treated directionally rather than as exact like-for-like rankings.
The feedback sample is not a defect-rate or incidence-rate dataset; verbatims identify customer value themes but do not quantify prevalence beyond the provided topic statistics.

requirements.title: Low-attention adjustment of cruise following distance
requirements.statement: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust active-cruise following distance and related frequently used driver-assistance settings while driving without searching through nested screen menus or taking attention away from the road.
requirements.customer_value: Keeps common assistance adjustments fast, predictable and confidence-inspiring, reducing perceived distraction at moments when the driver needs attention on surrounding traffic.
requirements.current_offer_note: Current option list offers BMW Live Cockpit Plus with BMW Curved Display, BMW Operating System 8.5, BMW Controller and Intelligent Personal Assistant as standard. Driving Assistant Plus/Professional offer active speed regulation. However, the list does not state that following-distance changes are directly accessible without menu navigation, so this is an improvement/gap rather than a new feature family.

evidence.detail: "feels unsafe needing to go through menu screens to adjust how much distance to keep"
"changing the gap to the car ahead while driving is awkward"
"the tech is distracting... going into the screen takes my eyes off the road"
evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

evidence.detail: "physical switches and buttons again for commonly used features, to reduce distraction"
"Aktive Geschwindigkeitsregelung 30 – 180 km/h"
"Aktive Geschwindigkeitsregelung 30 – 210 km/h" and "Abstandsinformation"

evidence.ref: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps

evidence.detail: 2025 volume 75,000; 2030 volume 78,000; growth 4.0%
2025 volume 78,000; 2030 volume 80,000; growth 2.6%

assumptions: By the successor launch, active cruise and related driver-assistance functions will remain common and important in the 5 Series customer journey.

Customers will continue to expect safety-relevant driving adjustments to be possible with very low visual and cognitive load, regardless of whether the interaction is physical, voice-based, controller-based or screen-based.
China applicability is inferred from the PM-approved market scope and global premium-customer expectations, because no China-specific verbatims were provided for cruise-gap adjustment.
uncertainties: The current option list does not describe the exact current interaction path for changing following distance, so the gap severity cannot be verified from the option list alone.
No task-time, glance-time or distraction benchmark data is provided for following-distance adjustment.
No China verbatims identify whether Chinese customers experience the same cruise-gap friction despite positive infotainment ease-of-use study scores.
conflicting_evidence: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 81.7, mean 8.35/10.
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 80.6, mean 8.26/10, even though EU feedback G60-0595 reports awkward cruise-gap adjustment.
PM-approved insight notes that some customers praise the new main screen, while others want more hard keys and simpler paths.

customer_impact.justification: The cited verbatims directly connect menu use for following-distance adjustment with perceived unsafety and eyes-off-road distraction. Because this task occurs while driving, the customer impact is very high.

future_relevance.justification: Driver-assistance usage and digital cockpit complexity are likely to remain highly relevant over the next 3–5 years. Provided 2030 volumes remain material across EU, China and the US, so the issue affects large successor-program markets.

competitive_gap.justification: The current offer already includes controller/voice/display interfaces and active cruise in assistance packages, which partially addresses the need. The option list does not show a direct no-menu access path, but no competitor benchmark was provided, so the gap is judged moderate rather than proven high.

brand_fit.justification: Strong fit with BMW intuitive technology and driver confidence; it supports a premium, low-distraction driving experience and indirectly Sheer Driving Pleasure by reducing interaction friction while driving.

issues: US and EU verbatims directly support friction around changing active-cruise gap/following distance while driving.
China market inclusion is weakly supported; the China study cited is about general infotainment ease of use and is marked as not supporting the requirement.
The phrase "related frequently used driver-assistance settings" is broader than the direct evidence, which is mainly about following-distance/gap adjustment and general distraction from screen menus.
"Without ... taking attention away from the road" is too absolute; any interaction may require some attention. A more defensible formulation is low visual/cognitive demand.
Option-list and sales evidence support feature availability and market relevance, but not the usability problem or interaction depth.
evaluation.suggested_statement: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust active-cruise following distance, and other validated high-frequency driver-assistance settings, while driving through clear, low-attention access paths that avoid nested menu searching and minimize eyes-off-road time.
evaluation.change_reason: Keeps the customer value and solution neutrality, but narrows the broader driver-assistance claim to settings that are validated and replaces the absolute "without taking attention away" with a more credible low-attention/minimized-distraction standard.

requirements.title: Easy access to climate, audio and navigation tasks
requirements.statement: Customers in the US, EU and China shall be able to adjust everyday climate, radio/audio and navigation-display details during a trip through clear, predictable access paths that do not require digging through menu screens.
requirements.customer_value: Reduces frustration and perceived distraction for high-frequency comfort and infotainment actions, allowing customers to keep the cabin, media and route information under control while staying focused on driving.
requirements.current_offer_note: Current option list offers BMW Live Cockpit Plus with BMW Curved Display, BMW Operating System 8.5, navigation, BMW Controller, Intelligent Personal Assistant, DAB tuner, Connected Music and automatic climate control; Comfort Paket adds 4-zone climate control. These are relevant enablers, but the option list does not state that common climate, radio/audio and navigation details are reachable without screen-hunting, so the need is an HMI improvement on top of existing functions.

evidence.ref: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps

evidence.detail: 2025 volume 75,000; 2030 volume 78,000; growth 4.0%
2025 volume 78,000; 2030 volume 80,000; growth 2.6%

assumptions: By the successor launch, the number of in-car apps and digital functions will not decrease, making clear access paths for core functions more important.

The customer need is solution-neutral: some customers explicitly ask for physical controls, but the requirement can also be met by any interaction concept that is fast, predictable and low-distraction.
Although the strongest negative evidence is from the US, the need is assumed to matter in EU and China as a premium baseline expectation for everyday operability.
uncertainties: No China verbatims identify which specific controls Chinese customers still find difficult despite good infotainment ease-of-use scores.
No objective task-time, glance-time or menu-depth benchmark is provided for climate, radio/audio or navigation-detail changes.
The option list confirms availability of climate, media and navigation functions, but does not describe their exact interaction depth or voice-control reliability.
conflicting_evidence: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 81.7, mean 8.35/10.
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 80.6, mean 8.26/10.
PM-approved insight notes that some customers praise the new main screen, while others want more hard keys and simpler paths.

customer_impact.justification: Climate, audio and navigation-detail changes are frequent everyday tasks, and multiple US verbatims/studies point to distraction or menu-friction. The impact is high, though less safety-critical than adjusting driver-assistance distance while in traffic.

future_relevance.justification: Digital cockpit scope and in-car apps are likely to expand over the next 3–5 years, so customers will value easier access to core tasks. The target markets also remain sizeable in the 2030 sales outlook.

competitive_gap.justification: BMW already offers a controller, voice assistant, curved display and connected infotainment, so there is a partial current answer. However, customer evidence still asks for simpler paths and a better analog/digital mix; without competitor data, the external competitive gap is judged moderate.

brand_fit.justification: Good fit with intuitive technology and premium quality: everyday comfort, media and navigation controls should feel clear, predictable and effortless in a BMW cabin.

issues: US evidence is reasonably supportive: multiple feedback items and US customer-study scores indicate issues with climate controls and infotainment menu structure.
EU and China evidence is weak for the stated pain point; the cited EU/CN studies show positive general infotainment ease-of-use results and are marked as not supporting the requirement.
Option-list evidence confirms that climate, navigation and audio features exist, but does not prove that access paths are difficult or nested.
The requirement partially overlaps REQ-01 because both address low-distraction access to commonly used driving-time functions, though the functional domains are different.
Some evidence asks for physical controls, but the statement is appropriately solution-neutral and does not mandate buttons.
evaluation.suggested_statement: Customers shall be able to adjust high-frequency climate, audio and navigation-view tasks during a trip through clear, predictable access paths that avoid unnecessary menu searching and minimize driver distraction.
evaluation.change_reason: The revised statement remains customer-facing and solution-neutral while avoiding the over-specific US/EU/China evidence claim until EU and China pain-point validation is available.

requirements.title: Simple charging-setting access for electrified 5 Series use
requirements.statement: Customers in the US, EU and China who drive electrified 5 Series variants shall be able to view and change everyday charging preferences without searching across multiple in-car menus.
requirements.customer_value: Makes electrified ownership easier by keeping charging-related decisions clear and accessible when preparing for a trip, arriving at a charger or managing daily charging routines.
requirements.current_offer_note: Current option list includes fully electric i5 and plug-in hybrid variants, charging hardware such as Ladekabel Professional and AC-Laden Professional, plus ConnectedDrive/Remote Services. It does not describe how easily customers can access charging settings in the vehicle, so this is an HMI clarity gap/unclear area rather than evidence of missing charging capability.

evidence.detail: "the tech is distracting... going into the screen takes my eyes off the road"
evidence.verification: partially verified: ID exists, quote paraphrased

evidence.detail: Vehicle range includes "VOLLELEKTRISCH" i5 variants and "PLUG-IN-HYBRID" 530e/550e variants
"Ladekabel Professional (Mode 3) für öffentliches Laden" listed for electrified variants
"AC-Laden Professional (22 kW)" listed as standard/optional depending on i5 variant
Includes "Remote Services" and "Connected Navigation"

evidence.ref: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps

evidence.detail: 2025 volume 75,000; 2030 volume 78,000; growth 4.0%
2025 volume 78,000; 2030 volume 80,000; growth 2.6%

assumptions: Electrified 5 Series variants will remain important in the successor generation, making charging-setting usability relevant over the next 3–5 years.
Customers will continue to expect charging preferences to be manageable in the vehicle even if some charging tasks are also handled through remote services or smartphone apps.
The charging-setting need is inferred from the PM-approved insight description and general menu-structure evidence; no charging-specific verbatim was provided.
uncertainties: Evidence for charging settings is thin: no feedback quote specifically mentions charging-setting menu friction.
Needs may differ materially between BEV and PHEV customers, and between home, workplace and public charging contexts.
Future remote-app capabilities may reduce how often customers need to change charging settings inside the vehicle.
The current option list confirms charging capability but not the actual in-car interaction flow.
conflicting_evidence: STUDY:CN:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 81.7, mean 8.35/10.
STUDY:EU:Easy to use information and entertainment system including in-car apps is positive at 80.6, mean 8.26/10.
No charging-specific negative verbatim was provided, so the requirement rests partly on extrapolation from general menu-friction evidence.

customer_impact.justification: For electrified-variant customers, charging-setting clarity can materially reduce ownership friction, but the task is less universally frequent than climate or cruise controls. The impact is therefore moderate with potential to be high for BEV-heavy use cases.

future_relevance.justification: Electrified variants are already central in the current 5 Series offer, and charging management is likely to remain relevant for the successor generation. Future relevance is high, but exact importance depends on drivetrain mix and remote-app adoption.

competitive_gap.justification: The current offer already contains electrified models, charging equipment and Remote Services, and no competitor benchmark or charging-specific complaint was provided. The gap is therefore judged low-to-moderate and mainly concerns interaction clarity rather than feature existence.

brand_fit.justification: The topic fits intuitive technology and sustainability for electrified ownership, but the requirement is less strongly evidenced and less clearly tied to a distinctive BMW experience than the first two.

issues: No cited feedback specifically mentions charging-setting access, charging preferences or charging-menu friction.
The main supporting customer evidence is general US infotainment menu-structure dissatisfaction, which only indirectly supports a charging-settings requirement.
China and EU customer-study evidence is marked as not supporting the requirement and does not identify a charging-specific problem.
Option-list evidence confirms electrified variants and charging equipment, but not customer difficulty with charging settings or in-car access paths.
The requirement is customer-facing and mostly solution-neutral, but needs stronger evidence across BEV/PHEV use cases and across US, EU and China before decision.
evaluation.suggested_statement: Electrified 5 Series customers shall be able to view and change common charging preferences through a clear, consolidated in-car access path.
evaluation.change_reason: This is shorter, more customer-facing and avoids the stronger unsupported claim about customers currently searching across multiple menus, while preserving the intended usability outcome.

portfolio_notes: REQ-01 and REQ-02 overlap around low-distraction access to frequently used in-trip functions; keep them separate only if driver-assistance controls and comfort/infotainment controls will be owned and validated as distinct journeys.

Market balance is uneven: the strongest negative evidence is US, with some EU support for REQ-01. China is included in all three requirements but has no direct pain-point verbatims; cited China study evidence is generally positive and does not support the claimed frictions.

REQ-03 is the weakest item. Before portfolio prioritization, gather charging-specific evidence by market and by BEV vs PHEV customer context, including home, public and trip-preparation charging scenarios.
Across all three requirements, option lists and sales data are useful for relevance and availability but should not be treated as evidence of customer usability pain.

A missing portfolio need is objective usability validation: task success, menu depth, glance time, voice/controller reliability and perceived confidence for the key tasks would help convert these into decision-ready requirements.
